reasoning_evidence: Signed IA Exhibit B (sources/2026-07-19_puct_35077-2307_standard-generation-interconnection-agreement-be.pdf, p.29): Scheduled Commercial Operation Date = September 20, 2027 - EXACT MATCH to queue-reported COD. In-Service Date May 13 2027, Trial Operation May 23 2027.

Queue timeline.md: 1 prior COD slip, 2027-01-30 -> 2027-09-20, noted at 2025-07-01 snapshot (~8mo slip) - this slip landed the queue COD exactly on the IA's contractual Scheduled COD, i.e. queue was updated to match the signed IA.

EIA-860M (eia_history.json): planned COD moved 2027-01 (through 2026-02 snapshot) -> 2027-10 (2026-03 onward) - EIA's own planned COD ALSO slipped ~9 months, landing close to (1 month after) the IA's Sept 2027 date. Two independent sources (signed IA, EIA-860M) now converge within 1 month of each other, both after a slip.

TotalEnergies press release (2026-02-09): construction on Mustang Creek scheduled to begin Q2 2026 — roughly 15-16 months of construction lead before the May 2027 In-Service Date, plausible for a 150 MW solar+BESS site but with limited slack.

Status caveat: EIA-860M still reports 'Not under construction' as of the May 2026 snapshot (i.e. the month the announced Q2 2026 window closes) - reporting lag likely, but if a real slip, pushes the whole schedule right.

Independent estimate nudges to 2027-Q4 (vs. reported 2027-09-20/Q3) because: (a) no imagery or Places confirmation of physical construction was obtainable this session despite the PR/hiring signal, so 'construction started on schedule' is not independently verified; (b) EIA planned-COD trend has moved later twice; (c) large solar+BESS co-located projects in this dataset (cf. Hanson Solar) have shown multi-month slips even after IA signature. Drift risk medium: strong contractual/financial grounding (signed IA, security posted and presumably paid, Google-backed developer) offset by zero independently-verified construction evidence.
